3

The KeePass application (keepass.html) opens, edits and creates KeePass password databases (.kdbx, KDBX 3.1 and 4). The files stay compatible with KeePass, KeePassXC, KeePassDX and other KeePass apps. Everything runs in the browser; nothing is sent over the network.

Unlocking a database

  1. Choose database… selects the .kdbx file. You can also drop the file (and its key file) onto the window. In Chrome/Edge on the desktop, Recently used lists the databases opened before.
  2. Enter the master password.
  3. If the database uses a key file, select it with Choose key file….
  4. Unlock. A wrong password or key file shows an error message.

Creating a database

Create a new database asks for a name and the master password (twice). Optionally, the application also creates a key file (<name>.keyx), which is downloaded immediately: keep it in a safe place, because without it the database cannot be opened. The new database is stored only after you save it.

Groups and entries

  • The left pane shows the groups. Click a group to show its entries; double-click a group (or Rename) to rename it. New group creates a subgroup of the selected group; Delete group moves the group with all its entries into the recycle bin.
  • The middle pane lists the entries of the group, sorted by title. The search field searches the title, user name, URL, notes and tags in all groups (Ctrl+F).
  • New entry creates an entry with a generated password in the selected group.
  • The right pane edits the selected entry. All changes take effect immediately; the Save button is highlighted while there are unsaved changes.

Editing an entry

Field Notes
Title, user name, URL, notes ⧉ copies the user name; Open opens the URL in a new tab
Password 👁 shows or hides it, ⧉ copies it; the strength is shown in bits
One-time password shown with its remaining seconds if the entry has an otp field (otpauth://totp/…, as written by KeePassXC)
Tags separated by commas
Expires sets an expiry date; expired entries are marked
Additional fields own fields with name and value; 🔒 protects a field (it is hidden and stored in encrypted form in memory)
Attachments add files, download them by clicking the name, or remove them
Group moves the entry into another group
History earlier versions of the entry; Restore makes an earlier version current again

Each time you edit an entry, the previous version is stored once in the history (not on every key press).

Copied values are removed from the clipboard after 30 seconds.

Undo (↶, Ctrl+Z) and redo (↷, Ctrl+Y) cover all changes to the database since it was unlocked: fields, new and deleted entries and groups, moving, attachments and settings. Typing into one field counts as one step. Locking clears the history.

↗ next to an attachment (Open with…) opens it in another application of the suite; saving there replaces the attachment. Save the database afterwards.

Password generator

🎲 Generate opens the generator: length (4 to 64), lower case, upper case, digits, symbols, and the option to avoid similar characters (l, 1, O, 0). ⟳ creates a new password; Use sets it as the password of the entry.

Recycle bin

Deleted entries and groups are moved into the Recycle bin group. To restore an entry, select it in the recycle bin and choose another group in the Group field. Empty recycle bin deletes its content permanently.

Saving

Save (Ctrl+S) writes the database directly into the opened file in Chrome/Edge on the desktop. In Firefox and on Android, the database is downloaded: replace the original file with it. Ctrl+Shift+S saves under a new name. After writing, the application checks that the saved file can be opened again.

Master key and database settings

Database opens the settings: the database name and Change master key (new password and, optionally, a new key file or removal of the existing key file). Save the database afterwards; keep the old file until you have checked that you can open the new one.

Merging databases

⇄ Merge… combines another .kdbx file with the open database (you enter its password and, if needed, its key file):

  • A copy of the same database (for example one edited on another computer or phone) is synchronized: for every entry the newer version wins, the older one goes into its history; new entries and groups are added and entries deleted in one copy are deleted. This is the same as "Synchronize" in KeePass and KeePassXC.
  • Another database is imported: its groups and entries are copied into a new group named after it (the recycle bin is skipped). Nothing in the open database is changed.

Save afterwards to keep the result; ↶ undoes the merge.

Password report

🩺 Report checks all entries (except those in the recycle bin) and lists problems: empty passwords, weak passwords (less than 60 bits of estimated strength, the same estimate as in the generator), passwords used in several entries, expired entries and passwords unchanged for more than a year (from the entry history). Click an entry to open it. The check runs completely in the browser; no password leaves the device.

Locking

Lock (Ctrl+L) closes the database; unsaved changes require a confirmation. After 15 minutes without activity the database is locked automatically, unless there are unsaved changes.

Keyboard shortcuts

On a Mac, use Cmd instead of Ctrl. F1 (or ?) shows this list in the application.

Files

Keys Function
Ctrl+S Save
Ctrl+Shift+S Save as
Ctrl+L Lock

Editing

Keys Function

On phones and tablets

The application shows one pane at a time: the entry list, a group list (‹ Groups) and the entry (‹ Entries goes back).
